summary: Configured inventory-worker on node1 as an enabled, long-running systemd service. It writes heartbeat data only under /var/lib/inventory, runs without capabilities, and has NoNewPrivileges enabled. The service and data recovered successfully after a verified node restart.
actions_performed: Created a dedicated inventory-worker system account and protected /var/lib/inventory directory.
Installed and enabled inventory-worker.service with strict filesystem, device, network, namespace, and privilege restrictions.
Verified heartbeat progress and tested write confinement from the service mount namespace.
Restarted node1 safely and confirmed a changed boot identity.
Verified post-restart service activation, heartbeat progress, data persistence, and sandbox enforcement.

evidence.requirement: Run inventory-worker as a managed, long-running background service
evidence.summary: Shows the unit enabled and active, a stable worker process, advancing heartbeat data, and automatic startup after reboot.
Live mount-namespace tests allowed writes under /var/lib/inventory while blocking /etc, /tmp, /run, and /var/tmp, both before and after restart.
The live process reports NoNewPrivs=1 with empty bounding and ambient capability sets; systemd confirms NoNewPrivileges=yes.

evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart and recovery sequence
evidence.summary: Captures healthy baseline boot ID 34027437-307c-4f58-bdb2-1fe626bb2d66, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID e7476fb1-c63b-4acf-a838-8694853801dd, and recovered service, data, heartbeat, and confinement state.
